evidence: AUTHORED FOR THIS PRODUCT: Template placeholders are fully replaced (template instruction.md is 'CHANGE_ME'; task.toml line 'name = "turing/hireops-recruiting-operations"', a HireOps-specific description, difficulty_explanation, provenance 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task as a recruiting workspace, with an authored reference implementation and browser rubric.', arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations'). Grep of the whole frozen task for other product names (pellmoor, colderwater, bazaar, ridgeline, torquebay, docketlight, boardloom, threadline, gridforge, patchpad, change-me, vacancy, merchant, playground, storefront, ballot, coursemark) returns nothing - no copy-paste residue. The brief and rules are written in the requester's voice with reasons, which also clears Colderwater lesson 12 for this row's 'reads as authored' half: instruction.md:1 'the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day ... the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled'; hireops_rules.md:50-51 'We like to know where a card was when it was rejected, because reopening takes it back to exactly that stage'; hireops_rules.md:126 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands'; hireops_rules.md:199 'Candidates are outside the company, so ...'; hireops_rules.md:206 'Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder'. Lesson 5's self-check line is present in product terms (instruction.md:13). Seed data is domain-specific (3 jobs JOB-PLAT/JOB-DATA/JOB-DSGN with interview_limit, 16 applications with stage/position, candidate_status_labels mapping, 127 messages incl. a 120-message paged thread whose '(#001)' suffixes serve paging, recruiter notes such as 'References checked. Compensation expectations within range.'); environment/assets/seed_data.json is byte-identical to solution/app/src/seed_data.json; UI <title> 'HireOps recruiting workspace'. All 56 criterion ids carry the task-specific 'hro_' prefix (functional 44, polish 5, visual 5, gates 2) and name HireOps mechanics (hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_undo_conflict, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_seen, hro_drafts, hro_candidate_private). DISTINCT FROM SIBLINGS: The only same-domain sibling is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline (recruitment). Overlap is thematic, not a noun swap: both have a one-stage-at-a-time pipeline, a hiring-manager role, an activity record, a no-duplicate-per-job email rule, a capacity limit and an all-or-nothing batch. But the mechanics differ: Pellmoor's limit is offer/hired openings against reservations, its batch is reviewed batch *offers* with preview, and its core is panel assessment versioning, scores and a history-derived d3 funnel with 'Only the hiring manager moves candidates'; HireOps' limit is Interview places, its batch is a multi-stage move with undo-while-untouched, and its core is multi-user concurrency (card versions, 409 naming the colleague, optimistic move with rollback and focus retention), shared manual ordering within stages, 15-second live updates that preserve typing/focus/scroll, recruiter-candidate conversations with 30-message paging that holds the reader's place, per-person unread, seen marks and per-user drafts surviving session expiry, plus a candidate portal with stage-wording mapping and staff-data exclusion. None of Pellmoor's panel/assessment/funnel flows appear in HireOps, and none of HireOps' messaging/live/undo/ordering flows appear in Pellmoor, so 'same flows, same criteria, renamed entities' (the skill's defect definition) does not hold. Threadline (chat) shares unread/paging concepts but is a channel/thread team-chat product with reactions, pins, mentions and webhooks; HireOps' conversations are one-per-application staff-candidate threads with role-scoped participation and candidate-facing seen semantics. FITS THE DOMAIN PLAN: no other task in projects/ uses arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations' or the same product, and NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:203 asks for reused infrastructure with distinct domain behaviour, which this task does. Counterexample attempts for this row: (a) a 'clone' reading - mapping HireOps onto Pellmoor by renaming vacancy->job, offer capacity->interview places - fails because ~half of HireOps' criteria (conversations, unread, seen, drafts, candidate portal, live updates, ordering, undo) have no Pellmoor counterpart; (b) broken-app / conforming-alternative probes are not applicable to an authorship/distinctness row and are owned by other rows. Runtime evidence is not required to decide this row.
notes: Non-blocking observations (no defect claimed): (1) Two recruiting-pipeline tasks exist in the workspace (HireOps and Pellmoor); if both are delivered to the same customer they could be perceived as domain-adjacent because both include no-stage-skip, capacity and atomic-batch rules, but the scored mechanics are clearly different as argued above. (2) arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations' omits the stack prefix most siblings use (e.g. 'full-stack-node-express-sqlite-...'); harmless for distinctness and not a row-53 defect - any naming-convention concern belongs to identity/metadata rows. (3) No suite-level written 'domain plan' document was found beyond NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md section 'Choosing tasks and using successful references'; 'fits the domain plan' was judged against that guidance and the sibling slice list.
